request.spec:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A plan on a sheet may name one of the sheet's descendants (a sheet id on the plan form; PLAN_ADDED
gains sheet=<id> at its end; a sheet that is not a descendant is refused). Its claims are then
generated for the person of the same name on that sheet (none when there is no such person), by
that sheet's rules and written in that sheet's audit; the plan still counts what it made.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A plan can now name one of the sheet's descendants, and its claims are generated on that sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec. After that run I only added comment lines to two endpoint YAML files and didn't run the tests again.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** new migration `V115__plan_sheet.sql` adds a `target_sheet_id` column to `plan`; it is empty when the plan uses its own sheet.
- **Adding a plan:** the request takes a `sheet` field. A blank one means the plan's own sheet. `SavePlan` refuses any sheet that isn't a descendant, including the sheet's own id. A refusal shows the plan error and writes nothing to the store or the audit file. `PLAN_ADDED` ends with ` sheet=<id>` when a sheet is named; otherwise the line is unchanged.
- **Generating (`AddPlanClaims`):**
  - For a plan that names a sheet, claims go to the person with the same name on that sheet. If there's no such person, nothing is made.
  - Claims follow that sheet's rules (its settings, terms, holidays, periods and retirement checks) and are logged and audited on that sheet, as `CLAIM_ADDED`.
  - The plan still counts what it made.
- **Front end:** the plan form has a new `plan-form-sheet` input, and a plan's row shows its sheet when it has one.

**Decisions to check**
- **Which "today" limits the dates:** generation runs up to the plan's own sheet's today, not the descendant's. The test requires this: after the parent moves to 2026-03-12 it expects child claims dated 03-06 and 03-11, while the child's today is still 03-01.
- **Matching by name:** I used the existing `findByName`, which ignores case and also matches a person's alias.
- **Rollup lines:** when generating changes a descendant's figures, `ROLLUP` lines are written to that sheet's audit after its claims. The test's audit check had no `ROLLUP` lines for that sheet, so this went through without being tested either way.
- **Skipped sheets:** a descendant that is archived, or where the user is only a viewer, gets no claims, as the existing rule already does for the plan's own sheet.
